questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Wait until it is safe, then merge into traffic.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:

options.text: Alcohol.
Amphetamines.
Anger.
Driving with teenagers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol.
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving ability. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving as much as a 0.05% blood alcohol level. Being awake for 24 hours straight impairs driving as much as a 0.10% blood alcohol level.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone
Wrong way
Railroad crossing
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs are only used to show a no passing zone.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs that show upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs for hazards are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces the effect of alcohol on your driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of causing a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can damage your brain function and hurt your driving ability. Mixing alcohol with other drugs increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must travel at the speed indicated.
The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on this road is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the maximum legal speed for that road. When it rains, snows, or conditions are poor, you may need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: To be safe when crossing railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Listen and look both ways for trains coming from either direction before crossing. Never proceed unless you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.
Both A and B are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both A and B are true.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds increase the chance of death in a crash. At speeds above 80 mph, survival in a crash is almost impossible. Driving much slower than other traffic can also be dangerous because impatient drivers may make unsafe passing moves.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: The road is especially slippery right after rain starts.
Wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
Leave extra distance when stopping.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially when rain first begins. Your tires ride on a thin layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to prevent your tires from losing grip.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching.
Stop only if other cars are already in the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop, let others go first, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver behind you wants to pass. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them space to pass safely and quickly.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them space to pass safely and quickly.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them more space in front of your car to complete the pass safely and quickly.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the back window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the back window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your car before backing up. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Children and small objects are hard to see from your seat. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs show?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings. Drivers must yield to trains. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass from either direction. You can cross these lines only to turn left or pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter riders when it is safe.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to let children off, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
Speed up quickly.
Turn on your emergency lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm out and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Stay to the right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass from your direction.

questions.question: You reach an intersection blocked by traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly until traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car in front.
Wait outside the intersection until you can go all the way through.
Use your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait outside the intersection until you can go all the way through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is backed up on the other side. Wait until the road ahead is clear so you can drive all the way through without blocking the intersection.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, what should you do?

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way as on dry roads.
Stay farther away from the car ahead.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. Your car will take longer to stop than it does on dry roads.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around a truck or bus where you cannot be seen.
A special speed zone.
A road where music volume is restricted.
A television show.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around a truck or bus where you cannot be seen.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the back, and in the front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."
